meta.title: AIXTRON SE — Felix Grawert's MOCVD compound-semiconductor deposition franchise through the GaN power, SiC, and micro-LED cycles
meta.abstract: AIXTRON SE (Frankfurt Xetra: AIXA; SDAX index member) is the principal German metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) equipment supplier — its tools deposit the compound-semiconductor epitaxial layers (GaN, SiC, GaAs, InP) that go into power electronics, micro-LED displays, laser diodes, photonics, and RF devices. Headquartered in Herzogenrath near Aachen, Germany. Strategic narrative through 2024-2026 has centered on the GaN power electronics inflection (GaN-on-Si for automotive, data-center and consumer power), the SiC power equipment cycle, the still-uncertain micro-LED display thesis, and CEO Felix Grawert's leadership through the post-Schulte transition.

chapters.body:
## AIXTRON at a Glance

Four decades after its 1983 founding by employees of RWTH Aachen's Institute for Semiconductor Technology, AIXTRON SE had already survived one full capital cycle in LED MOCVD and, by 2025, was positioning for a second one in compound semiconductors for power and photonics. The shares traded in Frankfurt's Prime Standard under the ticker AIXA and, as of the 2025 annual report, were constituents of both MDAX and TecDAX. Headquartered in Herzogenrath near Aachen, the company had been led by Felix Grawert as Chairman of the Executive Board since 1 April 2021, after he joined the board in August 2017 and succeeded Bernd Schulte, who retired on 31 March 2021. [AIXTRON History](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/about-aixtron/history) [AIXTRON Executive Board](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/executive-board) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## Fiscal 2025 in Brief

Full-year 2025 revenue came in at €556.6 million, down 12% from €633.2 million in 2024. Order intake fell to €544.3 million from €596.4 million, while equipment backlog ended the year at €257.8 million. EBIT declined to €100.3 million from €131.2 million, taking EBIT margin to 18.0% from 20.7% a year earlier; free cash flow swung to €181.9 million from negative €72.4 million. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf)

| Metric | FY2024 | FY2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | €633.2m | €556.6m | −12% |
| Order intake | €596.4m | €544.3m | −9% |
| EBIT | €131.2m | €100.3m | −24% |
| EBIT margin | 20.7% | 18.0% | −2.7 pp |
| Gross margin | 41% | 40% | −1 pp |
| Free cash flow | −€72.4m | €181.9m | — |

The 18% EBIT margin masked a more meaningful shift in product mix. In 2025, systems revenue totalled €444.6 million, of which power electronics represented €254.9 million, or 57%; optoelectronics contributed €101.4 million, or 23%; and LED including Micro LED accounted for €65.4 million, or 15%. In 2024 the mix had been 55% power electronics, 28% LED/Micro LED and 12% optoelectronics. AIXTRON's 2024 annual report had already warned that the market launch of new Micro LED products was likely to be delayed by two to three years because of technological challenges; the 2025 report then showed that the elevated LED/Micro LED system demand of 2024 had not repeated. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf)

## The Platform Architecture

AIXTRON's revenue was built around distinct platform families. The 2025 annual report described the G10-GaN as a fully automated, compact MOCVD cluster tool for high-production power-electronics factories on 150 mm and 200 mm wafers, and management continued to tie its demand case to automotive power conversion, data-centre power supplies and fast chargers. In the same report, the company said Yole estimated AIXTRON's overall share of the compound-semiconductor MOCVD market at 77% in 2024. Publicly disclosed customer evidence around the frozen window included Nexperia's July 2024 order for G10-GaN tools alongside G10-SiC equipment, and Renesas's May 2026 expansion of high-volume GaN production using additional Planetary G5+C systems. [G10-GaN](https://www.aixtron.com/en/products/G10-GaN_p2739) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [Nexperia order](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Nexperia%20partners%20with%20AIXTRON%20for%20200mm%20SiC%20and%20GaN%20power_n12625) [Renesas order](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20supplied%20Planetary%20GaN%20MOCVD%20Systems%20to%20Renesas%20for%20High-Volume%20Manufacturing%20Expansion_n13970)

The G10-SiC platform was younger and more contested. AIXTRON marketed it as a dual-wafer-size batch reactor for 150 mm and 200 mm SiC epitaxy, with a 9x150 mm and 6x200 mm configuration, and its 2025 annual report said Yole put AIXTRON's 2024 share of the SiC CVD systems market at about 27%, versus 32% for ASM and 16% for Tokyo Electron. Public disclosures around the frozen window were more specific than the draft implied: Nexperia said in July 2024 that it was placing a repeat order for G10-SiC for its 200 mm SiC volume ramp, and AIXTRON said on 22 September 2025 that it had shipped its 100th G10-SiC system to a European power-device and systems manufacturer. [G10-SiC](https://www.aixtron.com/de/produkte/verbindungshalbleiter-mocvd/g10-sic) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [Nexperia order](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Nexperia%20partners%20with%20AIXTRON%20for%20200mm%20SiC%20and%20GaN%20power_n12625) [100th G10-SiC shipment](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20achieves%20100th%20G10-SiC%20Shipment%20Milestone_n13801)

The third platform vector was optoelectronics. In October 2025, AIXTRON told investors that the G10-AsP was 'establishing itself as the tool of record to the laser market', and subsequent disclosed orders underscored the point: Nokia took a G10-AsP system for next-generation photonics in April 2025, and Lumentum placed multiple G10-AsP orders in May 2026 for AI-network optical connectivity. [Q3 2025 transcript](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/events/telefonkonferenz/2025/AIXTRON_SE_Q3_2025_transcript.pdf) [Nokia order](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20delivers%20G10-AsP%20for%20production%20of%20next%20generation%20photonics%20to%20Nokia_n13685) [Lumentum order](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20receives%20multiple%20orders%20for%20G10-AsP%20MOCVD%20Systems%20from%20Lumentum%20to%20support%20expansion%20of%20High-Speed%20Optical%20Solutions%20for%20AI%20Networks_n13987)

## The 2026 Inflection

A first-quarter 2026 order surge changed the tenor of the year. On 14 April 2026, AIXTRON said preliminary Q1 order intake had risen about 30% year-on-year to about €171 million, with more than 65% of equipment orders tied to optoelectronics; the subsequent quarterly statement put reported Q1 order intake at €171.4 million. At the same time the company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to around €560 million in a range of plus or minus €30 million from a prior €520 million, and lifted its EBIT margin guidance to 17% to 20% from 16% to 19%. [AIXTRON guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20increases%20FY%202026%20guidance%20and%20reports%20preliminary%20Q1/2026%20figures_n13936) [Q1/2026 Quarterly Statement](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2026/englisch/3-Months-Report-2026.pdf)

> "The significantly stronger-than-expected demand from the Optoelectronics sector in the first quarter is a very encouraging development... With our G10-AsP system, we have the tool of record for the next generation of photonic components." — Felix Grawert, 14 April 2026 [AIXTRON guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20increases%20FY%202026%20guidance%20and%20reports%20preliminary%20Q1/2026%20figures_n13936)

GaN power, by contrast, was described in the Q1 2026 management speech as "stable but soft", while SiC market conditions were said to have remained soft amid industry underutilisation. The company nevertheless argued that its installed base and cost-of-ownership profile left it well positioned for the next leg of both ramps. [Q1/2026 results speech](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/events/telefonkonferenz/2026/Q1-2026%20Results%20Speech.pdf)

> "We expect that AI data centers can become the largest single application for GaN power semiconductors in the near future." — Felix Grawert, Annual Report 2025 [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## What the Dossier Asks

The forward research questions that animate this dossier are tightly bounded. How durable was the GaN power inflection once AI data-centre power-delivery architectures shifted toward higher-density rack designs? Could AIXTRON defend or expand its SiC position against ASM/LPE, Tokyo Electron and Veeco as the 200 mm transition compressed incumbent advantages? What residual value remained in the micro-LED thesis after AIXTRON itself said commercial launches had slipped by two to three years? How did German two-tier governance — Vorstand under Grawert, Aufsichtsrat above — shape capital allocation at a company carrying €272.7 million of cash and other current financial assets at 31 March 2026? And how exposed was a euro-reporting, globally selling equipment company to a weaker dollar? [Q1/2026 Quarterly Statement](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2026/englisch/3-Months-Report-2026.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf)

chapters.title: From 1983 RWTH Aachen spin-off through LED cycles to GaN power and SiC inflection
chapters.body:
## Aachen's Compound-Semiconductor Laboratory, 1983

The company that would become Europe's pre-eminent maker of compound-semiconductor deposition equipment began not in a boardroom but in RWTH Aachen's semiconductor laboratories. AIXTRON's own history page said the business was founded in 1983 by employees of the Institute for Semiconductor Technology at RWTH Aachen; the founders it names are Heinrich Schumann, Holger Jurgensen and Meino Heyen. The name itself came from Aix-la-Chapelle, the French name for Aachen, combined with 'electronics'. [AIXTRON History](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/about-aixtron/history)

Herzogenrath, adjacent to RWTH Aachen, became the company's permanent manufacturing base. AIXTRON's official chronology added two milestones that explained how quickly the spin-out industrialised: an exclusive licence from Philips for Planetary Reactor technology in 1989 and the company's Frankfurt IPO in 1997. [AIXTRON History](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/about-aixtron/history)

Through the 1980s and into the early 1990s, the business served a niche: research institutes, defence-linked compound-semiconductor fabs, and early optoelectronic device manufacturers buying systems capable of growing gallium arsenide, indium phosphide, and related III-V materials. Revenue was measured in tens of millions of euros and the customer roster was small. The key technological advance of those years was the multi-wafer planetary reactor concept, which allowed simultaneous epitaxial growth across multiple wafers by rotating each wafer around its own axis on a gas-cushion bearing — a design that would underpin every subsequent product generation.

## The LED Decade and Its Aftermath

The transformational event for AIXTRON came from an unexpected direction. As solid-state lighting and consumer displays drove adoption of gallium nitride LEDs through the 2000s, the demand for MOCVD reactors capable of growing GaN on sapphire substrates exploded. Asian device manufacturers — initially in Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea, then in rapidly expanding volume in mainland China — needed precisely the multi-wafer planetary reactors that AIXTRON had spent two decades refining. The company's AIX 2000 and successor systems became standard equipment in LED chip fabs across the region.

Between roughly 2007 and 2011, AIXTRON's revenues scaled sharply as Chinese LED manufacturers, backed by regional subsidies and aggressive capacity targets, placed equipment orders at a pace the industry had never seen. The company's own 2011 annual report showed revenue of €783.8 million in 2010 and €611.0 million in 2011, still its second-best year to that point even after a violent late-cycle slowdown and backlog adjustment. For a company headquartered in a small German city, the growth was dizzying. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2011](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2011/en/Annual%20Report%202011.pdf)

The correction was equally severe. By 2012 and 2013, Chinese LED fabs had built far more capacity than the nascent solid-state lighting market could absorb. New orders collapsed, utilisation rates at customer facilities fell sharply, and AIXTRON's order intake entered a multi-year trough. Revenue declined toward the €150–€200 million range and the company posted losses. The LED boom had made AIXTRON; the LED bust exposed an uncomfortable concentration risk in a single application and a single geography.

The episode left marks on how subsequent management would think about portfolio construction. The dependence on Chinese LED volume customers — firms whose buying behaviour was driven as much by subsidy cycles and local government directives as by genuine equipment demand — proved difficult to forecast and impossible to hedge. A company whose core technology was broadly applicable to multiple compound-semiconductor applications had allowed itself to be defined, for a critical window, almost entirely by one of them.

The vulnerability became acute in 2016 when Grand Chip Investment GmbH, backed by Fujian Grand Chip Investment Fund LP, launched its takeover attempt. AIXTRON's own disclosures recorded two separate interventions: on 24 October 2016 the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy withdrew the clearance certificate it had previously issued, and on 3 December 2016 the U.S. President prohibited the acquisition of AIXTRON's U.S. business after the CFIUS process. The bid collapsed, and the episode became an early marker of the broader Western turn toward tighter scrutiny of strategic semiconductor assets. [AIXTRON, 24 October 2016](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20Withdrawal%20of%20Clearance%20Certificate%20and%20reopening%20of%20review%20proceedings%20by%20the%20Ministry%20of%20Economics%20pertaining%20to%20the%20takeover%20by%20Grand%20Chip%20Investment%20GmbH_n894) [AIXTRON, 3 December 2016](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/AIXTRON%20SE%20Tender%20Offer%20by%20Grand%20Chip%20Investment%20GmbH%20/%20Prohibition%20of%20Acquisition%20of%20U.S.%20Business%20of%20AIXTRON%20by%20the%20U.S.%20President_n892)

## Grawert and the Strategic Rebuild, 2017–2023

Felix Grawert arrived at AIXTRON in August 2017 after serving at Infineon Technologies, where he had run the high-voltage-conversion product line, and before that at McKinsey. He joined the Executive Board while Bernd Schulte remained in office, giving the company a handover period that combined Schulte's operating memory with Grawert's power-semiconductor background. The formal transition came later than the draft suggested: Schulte retired on 31 March 2021 and the Supervisory Board appointed Grawert Chairman of the Executive Board with effect from 1 April 2021. [AIXTRON Executive Board](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/executive-board) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2021](https://aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2021/en/Annual%20Report-2021.pdf)

The pivot had a clear logic. GaN-on-silicon and GaN-on-SiC power electronics were entering a commercialisation phase after years of laboratory development. The physical properties of gallium nitride — higher breakdown voltage, faster switching speed, and lower on-resistance than silicon — made it attractive for power conversion applications in electric-vehicle onboard chargers, data-centre power supply units, and high-efficiency consumer adapters. SiC power devices served an overlapping but distinct segment, with particular strength in high-voltage traction inverters for electric vehicles and grid-connected power systems. Both application areas required MOCVD epitaxial growth equipment. AIXTRON already had the reactor design competence; the question was whether the commercial markets would develop on a timescale relevant to the company's planning horizon.

The product platform that emerged from this period was the G10 series — a family of large-format multi-wafer planetary reactors optimised for GaN-on-silicon and, subsequently, SiC epitaxy. The G10-GaN and G10-SiC tools represented a deliberate move up the performance and pricing curve, targeting production-scale fabs building capacity for power electronics rather than the lower-margin research and LED markets. The parallel G5 platform continued to serve GaAs, InP, and speciality compound-semiconductor applications including laser diodes for datacom transceivers, VCSELs for 3D-sensing modules, and automotive LiDAR sources.

Schulte's retirement came earlier than the draft stated. AIXTRON's 2021 annual report recorded that he left the Executive Board on 31 March 2021 after nineteen years, with Christian Danninger joining as CFO on 1 May 2021 and Jochen Linck remaining COO until 30 September 2023. From October 2023 onward, the board consisted of Grawert and Danninger, overseen by the Supervisory Board within Germany's two-tier governance structure. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2021](https://aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2021/en/Annual%20Report-2021.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf)

## The GaN Power and SiC Inflection, 2023–2025

The years between 2023 and 2025 validated, at least partially, the strategic thesis that Grawert had been constructing since his arrival. G10-GaN system shipments scaled as device manufacturers — ranging from Infineon and STMicroelectronics in Europe to Wolfspeed and Navitas in North America and Innoscience in China — invested in GaN-on-silicon epitaxial capacity. The adoption curve in consumer power adapters, driven by the proliferation of USB Power Delivery and gallium nitride charger designs from brands including Anker and Belkin, had produced a tangible volume pull-through that justified production-scale reactor investment.

Data-centre power conversion added a structurally larger demand vector. The accelerating buildout of AI compute infrastructure placed unprecedented demand on power delivery efficiency, and GaN-based power factor correction and conversion designs offered meaningful efficiency gains that hyperscale operators translated directly into operating-cost reductions at the data-centre level. By the time AIXTRON reported its fiscal 2024 results, revenue had reached €633.2 million — still below the 2010 LED-era peak of €783.8 million, but close enough to show that the company had rebuilt scale on a broader application base and with materially higher average selling prices per system. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2011](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2011/en/Annual%20Report%202011.pdf)

SiC entered the revenue mix more slowly, reflecting the longer qualification cycles and the entrenched position of existing SiC epitaxy suppliers in a market that Wolfspeed and others had structured around proprietary process relationships. The G10-SiC platform was commercialised and shipped, but its contribution to total order intake through 2024 remained modest relative to GaN.

The one application that had been expected to contribute materially — and did not — was micro-LED display. AIXTRON's own 2024 annual report said the market launch of new Micro LEDs was expected to be delayed by two to three years because of technological challenges. The thesis was not abandoned — the physics of display-grade III-V epitaxy still mattered — but its contribution to AIXTRON's planning horizon receded into a longer-dated, more speculative position, leaving GaN power, SiC and optoelectronics as the principal growth levers entering 2025 and beyond. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf)

chapters.title: G10-GaN, G10-SiC, photonics MOCVD, broader compound-semi equipment
chapters.body:
## The G10 Platform: AIXTRON's Power Electronics Engine

The G10-GaN reactor sat at the centre of AIXTRON's commercial renaissance in power electronics. The annual reports described it as a fully automated, compact MOCVD cluster tool for high-production power-electronics factories on 150 mm and 200 mm wafers, while the current product material emphasised seamless process transfer from the earlier AIX G5+ C. What mattered for the dossier was not the branding nuance but the manufacturing aim: high-throughput GaN epitaxy for power and RF applications at industrial scale. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [G10-GaN](https://www.aixtron.com/en/products/G10-GaN_p2739)

The commercial case for the tool converged with a structural shift in power conversion. AIXTRON's own power-management material highlighted automotive, data-centre, consumer, solar and industrial applications as the key demand vectors for GaN and SiC power devices, while company disclosures through 2024 and 2025 repeatedly tied the GaN build-out to higher-efficiency power supplies and converters. Device manufacturers across Asia, Europe and North America were therefore buying into a multi-year installed-base story rather than a one-off lab cycle. [Power management](https://www.aixtron.com/en/innovation/applications/power-management) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

Order-intake geography confirmed the breadth of adoption. Chinese GaN power device makers, spurred by government-backed semiconductor self-sufficiency programmes, represented a meaningful share of G10-GaN order flow through 2023 and into 2024. The concentration introduced customer-mix risk, but it also validated the platform's positioning as the reference tool for a nascent production ecosystem.

## G10-SiC: Staking a Claim Against CVD Incumbents

The G10-SiC programme represented a deliberate stretch into territory historically dominated by hot-wall chemical vapour deposition equipment suppliers — a different MOCVD-adjacent market where AIXTRON's reactor expertise offered a differentiated entry point rather than incumbency.

Silicon carbide epitaxy for power devices had long been served by specialised SiC CVD suppliers, most notably LPE before its acquisition by ASM. AIXTRON's proposition with G10-SiC was that a warm-wall planetary approach could combine very high deposition temperatures with a batch reactor's throughput and cost profile. The company marketed the system as a 150/200 mm dual-wafer-size platform with 9x150 mm and 6x200 mm capability, while its 2025 annual report said Yole placed AIXTRON's 2024 share of the SiC CVD systems market at about 27%. [ASM-LPE announcement](https://www.asm.com/press-releases/asm-announces-agreement-to-acquire-lpe-entering-high-growth-silicon-carbide-epitaxy-equipment-business-2480778) [G10-SiC](https://www.aixtron.com/de/produkte/verbindungshalbleiter-mocvd/g10-sic) [Warm-wall planetary principle](https://www.aixtron.com/en/innovation/technologies/warm-wall-planet-principle) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

The commercial stakes were substantial. Wolfspeed, STMicroelectronics, Infineon, and a cohort of Chinese SiC makers including SICC and TankeBlue were all constructing SiC epitaxy capacity ahead of anticipated electric-vehicle drivetrain demand in the 2025–2028 window. Even a modest share of the SiC epi-tool market — considerably larger in aggregate capital expenditure than the GaN power segment — would represent a material revenue diversification for a company whose revenue base was roughly EUR 600 million in 2024.

Grawert was measured about the SiC timeline in public communications, acknowledging that displacing established hot-wall CVD tools in a conservative, automotive-qualified supply chain required demonstrating defect density and run-to-run repeatability at production scale, not just in application laboratories. The G10-SiC entered early customer qualification cycles during 2023 and 2024, with commercial shipments tracking behind the GaN platform's ramp but accumulating process data that management described as encouraging. The disclosed evidence by the frozen date was no longer hypothetical: Wolfspeed said in April 2024 that it had placed multiple-tool orders in the second half of 2023 to support its 200 mm production plans, and Nexperia followed with a repeat order in July 2024. [Wolfspeed selects AIXTRON tools](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Wolfspeed%20Selects%20AIXTRON%20Tools%20to%20Support%20200mm%20Production_n12560) [Nexperia order](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Nexperia%20partners%20with%20AIXTRON%20for%20200mm%20SiC%20and%20GaN%20power_n12625)

| Platform | Substrate | Primary End Markets | Competitive Landscape | Status (as of 2024) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G10-GaN | GaN-on-Si, GaN-on-SiC | Auto OBC, data-centre PSU, fast charge | Veeco and in-house epi lines | Commercial scale by 2025 |
| G10-SiC | SiC-on-SiC | EV drivetrain inverters, industrial | ASM/LPE, Tokyo Electron, Veeco | Commercial ramp with disclosed repeat orders |
| G5+ / G10-AsP photonics | GaAs, InP | Datacom lasers, VCSELs, LiDAR | Specialist photonics MOCVD peers | Mature/stable, with renewed opto momentum |

## Photonics MOCVD: The Quiet Annuity

While the G10 power platforms attracted the bulk of investor attention, AIXTRON's photonics MOCVD franchise continued to generate steady equipment orders and aftermarket revenue from a geographically diversified customer base that had been constructing datacom and sensing capacity with G5-series tools for more than a decade.

The photonics segment spans three primary application clusters. Datacom transceivers — the edge-emitting laser diodes and electroabsorption-modulated lasers that carry 400G and 800G optical traffic inside hyperscale data centres — are grown on gallium arsenide and indium phosphide substrates in AIXTRON reactors operated by fabs aligned with II-VI/Coherent, Lumentum, and Sumitomo Electric. Automotive LiDAR brought a second demand vector: pulsed 905-nanometre edge-emitting lasers for time-of-flight ranging systems, where AIXTRON's GaAs epi tools were already qualified in the supply chains of Tier-1 automotive laser suppliers. VCSELs for consumer 3D sensing — the structured-light modules behind smartphone face-unlock and gesture-recognition systems — constituted a third, more volatile stream sensitive to platform upgrade cycles at handset OEMs.

The photonics book was not a growth story in the 2022–2025 period; it was a durability story. Datacom laser capacity builds tracked data-centre construction with a lag, and the VCSEL market oscillated with consumer electronics cycles. But the installed base of AIXTRON photonics reactors in customer fabs — each requiring periodic process-kit replacement, spare-part provisioning, and calibration services — generated recurring aftermarket revenue with margins structurally above the equipment sale. AIXTRON's services and spare-parts line, consolidated within its aftermarket reporting, provided a partial hedge against the lumpiness of new-tool orders across all product lines.

## Micro-LED: The Thesis Under Stress

No segment illustrated the asymmetry between thesis and execution more sharply than Micro LED display epitaxy. AIXTRON's own 2024 annual report said market launches for new Micro LEDs were likely to be delayed by two to three years because of technological challenges, and the 2025 annual report showed the effect in the numbers: LED including Micro LED represented 28% of equipment revenues in 2024 but only 15% of systems revenue in 2025. Display-panel makers kept funding research and pilot activity, but the large production wave long anticipated for 2024-2025 did not materialise. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

Grawert acknowledged the deceleration without abandoning the long-term thesis. The segment, he noted, remained technically compelling; the question was timing, not direction. The practical consequence for AIXTRON's medium-term revenue profile was a more concentrated dependence on power electronics — GaN power and, progressively, SiC — to sustain the revenue base that had been partially underwritten by micro-LED expectations.

## Aftermarket, Services, and the Recurring Revenue Layer

Across all tool families, AIXTRON's aftermarket and services business provided ballast against the capital-equipment cycle. The installed base of G5 and G10 reactors in customer fabs required a steady flow of process kits — susceptors, liners, inlet components — that degraded with use and required periodic replacement to maintain epi quality. Extended service agreements, remote diagnostics, and process-optimisation consulting added revenue streams that were structurally less volatile than equipment orders.

AIXTRON in fact disclosed more aftermarket detail than the draft suggested. Service, spare parts and related revenue amounted to €97.6 million in 2023, €110.7 million in 2024 and €112.0 million in 2025, equal to 15%, 17% and 20% of group revenue respectively. That did not give the same contract-by-contract granularity some U.S. peers provide, but it did show a steadily larger recurring layer as the installed base expanded. Each G10 tool shipped into a customer fab therefore implied a multi-year consumables and service relationship that partially smoothed the lumpier new-equipment order book. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

The aggregate picture by the frozen snapshot date in May 2026 was of a company whose product architecture had been substantially repositioned — from LED MOCVD toward GaN power, SiC power, and photonics — with micro-LED as a residual optionality rather than a near-term volume driver. The G10-GaN platform had achieved commercial scale; the G10-SiC was in qualification; photonics tools were a stable annuity; and micro-LED remained the chapter whose conclusion the industry had not yet written.

chapters.title: Revenue trajectory, order intake cyclicality, EBIT margin progression, capital allocation
chapters.body:
The four fiscal years from 2022 through 2025 trace the full arc of a compound-semiconductor capital-equipment cycle: the demand surge that carried AIXTRON from mid-tier profitability to its best-ever results, the plateau, and the controlled compression that followed as GaN power adoption paused and micro-LED display orders failed to materialise. Read in sequence, the numbers form a precise record of both the franchise's earnings power and the structural risks that attend a concentrated, capital-equipment business model exposed to the idiosyncratic buildout timelines of a handful of device chipmakers.

## The Revenue Surge and Its Arithmetic

The fiscal-year pivot came in 2023. After posting revenue of €463.2 million in FY2022, AIXTRON booked €629.9 million in FY2023, a 36% step-change that ranked as the company's strongest annual revenue growth in more than a decade. The company attributed the move to strong demand for MOCVD equipment for GaN and SiC power devices, while laser and LED demand recovered in the fourth quarter. FY2024 came in almost exactly flat at €633.2 million, showing that the surge had reached a plateau. The picture in FY2025 was more difficult: revenue contracted 12% to €556.6 million as GaN demand fell short of original expectations, LED/Micro LED demand remained weak, and FX moved against the company. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

| Fiscal Year | Revenue (€m) | YoY Change | EBIT (€m) | EBIT Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2022 | 463.2 | +8% | 104.7 | 22.6% |
| FY2023 | 629.9 | +36% | 156.8 | 24.9% |
| FY2024 | 633.2 | +1% | 131.2 | 20.7% |
| FY2025 | 556.6 | −12% | 100.3 | 18.0% |

*Sources: [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf); [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf); [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)*

## Order Intake Cyclicality and Backlog Dynamics

For a company whose revenues are delivered with a lag of six to eighteen months after booking, order intake and equipment backlog are the forward-facing vital signs. The FY2022 order intake of €585.9m—18 per cent above the prior year and the second-highest annual figure in AIXTRON's history at the time—seeded the FY2023 revenue surge. The FY2023 order intake of €640.7m, a further 9 per cent gain, signalled that FY2024 revenue would hold: it did, exactly. The deceleration that began in the second half of 2023 then manifested in the order line with a one-cycle lag. FY2024 order intake fell 7 per cent to €596.4m; FY2025 declined a further 9 per cent to €544.3m. Equipment order backlog—the unconverted portion of booked orders—peaked at €353.7m at the end of FY2023 and had eroded to €257.8m by end-FY2025, a 27 per cent drawdown over two years.

| Fiscal Year | Order Intake (€m) | Equipment Backlog (€m) |
|---|---|---|
| FY2022 | 585.9 | 351.8 |
| FY2023 | 640.7 | 353.7 |
| FY2024 | 596.4 | 289.3 |
| FY2025 | 544.3 | 257.8 |

The composition of the order book shifted substantially during this period. AIXTRON's regional revenue disclosures showed Asia accounting for 50% of sales in 2023, 66% in 2024 and 60% in 2025, underscoring how strongly the cycle remained tied to Asian customer capex even after the European power narrative strengthened. The quarter-end cadence also showed how shallow the recovery remained: order intake in Q4 2024 was €157.0 million, 9% above Q3 2024, while Q4 2025 improved further to €169.6 million, 37% above Q3 2025 and 8% above the prior-year quarter. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [AIXTRON FY2025 results](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20with%20robust%20results%20in%20a%20soft%20market%20environment_n13896)

A recurring revenue layer cushioned that order volatility more than the earlier draft acknowledged. Service, spare parts and related revenue rose from €97.6 million in 2023 to €110.7 million in 2024 and €112.0 million in 2025, lifting its share of group revenue from 15% to 20%. That did not neutralise the cycle, but it meant a larger slice of the P&L was tied to installed-base utilisation rather than fresh tool purchases. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) It also helped explain why the 2024-2025 slowdown looked like a plateau and compression cycle rather than a balance-sheet crisis.

## EBIT Margin Progression and Management's Implicit Targets

AIXTRON's EBIT margin trajectory across the four-year window illustrates the leverage—both positive and negative—inherent in a business with high operating costs and relatively sticky R&D expenditure. At the FY2022 EBIT margin of 22.6 per cent, the company already exceeded its publicly communicated guidance band of 20–23 per cent. The FY2023 result of 24.9 per cent sat at the lower end of a mid-year-upgraded guidance range of 25–27 per cent, reflecting a mix effect as volume pulled ahead of realised product-margin improvement. Management has not published a formally labelled "mid-cycle" or "through-cycle" EBIT margin target in the manner of, say, an industrial conglomerate issuing a Capital Markets Day framework; the closest functional equivalent is the 25 per cent level demonstrated in FY2023, which analysts and investors have treated as the proxy peak-cycle target.

The FY2024 compression from 24.9% to 20.7% reflected the interplay of product mix, heavier R&D and weaker end-market demand than management had initially expected. R&D rose to €91.4 million, and the company cut its FY2024 EBIT-margin guidance in July 2024 to 22% to 25% from 24% to 26% before ultimately reporting 20.7%. By the FY2025 results release, management was openly framing the next phase around restoring profitability and rebuilding cash. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Q2/2024 guidance update](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20reports%20preliminary%20Q2/2024%20results%20with%20strong%20order%20intake.%20Momentum%20in%20SiC%20and%20GaN%20power%20continues.%20Guidance%20for%202024%20adjusted._n12621) [AIXTRON FY2025 results](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20with%20robust%20results%20in%20a%20soft%20market%20environment_n13896)

The FY2025 EBIT margin of 18.0 per cent, landing at the midpoint of a final revised guidance range of 17–19 per cent, represented the lowest margin since the pre-GaN-power era. Grawert was characteristically measured about the near-term context:

> "In 2025 we have performed well in a soft market environment ... our free cash flow increased by more than EUR 250 million." — Felix Grawert, February 2026 [FY2025 results speech](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/events/telefonkonferenz/2026/FY-2025%20Results%20Speech.pdf)

The 2026 guidance issued in February 2026—subsequently raised in April 2026 to 17–20 per cent EBIT margin on revenue guidance of €560–620m—signalled that management regarded FY2025 as a trough rather than a reset, with the optoelectronics cycle, particularly AI-driven datacom laser tools, positioned as the primary recovery driver.

Seen another way, the FY2022-FY2025 margin arc also clarified what AIXTRON considered normal versus exceptional. The company could still produce EBIT margins above 20% while funding heavy R&D, but the 24.9% achieved in 2023 now looked less like a new floor than a peak earned under unusually favourable mix and utilisation conditions. That distinction mattered for valuation: investors anchoring on 2023 as a steady-state earnings level were implicitly assuming that both wide-bandgap power and Micro LED would ramp without interruption, a proposition the subsequent annual reports did not support. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## R&D Intensity and the Investment Cycle

One of the more instructive features of the FY2022–FY2025 data was the deliberate decision to maintain, and indeed accelerate, research and development expenditure through the revenue downturn. R&D climbed from €57.7 million in FY2022 to €91.4 million in FY2024 before stepping back to €81.1 million in FY2025, equal to roughly 15% of revenue in the latter year. The company tied those investments to the completion of the G10 product family, continuing SiC and GaN platform work, and the Herzogenrath Innovation Center, which management said would facilitate the leap to 300 mm wafers in GaN power electronics. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## Dividends, Buybacks, and Cash Allocation

The dividend history across the four years traced an arc that closely mirrored the net-income trajectory. AIXTRON paid €0.31 per share for FY2022 and raised that to €0.40 for FY2023, then cut the FY2024 dividend to €0.15 per share as earnings fell back. The FY2025 dividend proposal was again €0.15 per share. The payout policy therefore normalised to a more conservative level just as the company was digesting its Innovation Center investment, planning the Malaysia expansion and rebuilding liquidity. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [Q1/2026 Quarterly Statement](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2026/englisch/3-Months-Report-2026.pdf)

No active share buyback programme was in operation during FY2022–FY2024. At the May 2025 Annual General Meeting, shareholders authorised management to repurchase and cancel treasury shares, but no specific programme size or execution timeline had been disclosed by the frozen snapshot date of 23 May 2026. The authorisation exists as an option, not a commitment.

## Free Cash Flow and Balance Sheet Reconstruction

The free cash flow record over the period tells a more volatile story than the income statement alone suggests. FY2022 produced a modest free cash flow of €7.7 million despite strong profitability, as the working-capital cycle absorbed the order-intake surge in advance inventory. FY2023's €629.9 million revenue year generated negative free cash flow of €109.7 million, explained by CapEx for the Aachen Innovation Center and a substantial build in inventory as production ramped ahead of deliveries. FY2024 produced a further negative €72.4 million in free cash flow, compressing cash and equivalents to €64.6 million at year-end. The FY2025 reversal was dramatic: operating cash flow of €208.4 million and free cash flow of €181.9 million rebuilt the year-end cash line to €224.6 million, a recovery driven by inventory drawdown, lower CapEx and stronger customer prepayments. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

The Q1 2026 statement then showed how much of that reconstruction had carried into the new year even before revenues recovered. Working capital fell by more than €76 million from year-end 2025, advance payments received from customers rose to about €79 million, or roughly 22% of order backlog, and cash including other current financial assets climbed to €272.7 million as of 31 March 2026. The subsequent €450 million zero-coupon convertible bond gave management additional flexibility for growth investment, possible M&A and buybacks, but it also underlined that balance-sheet repair had become part of the earnings story, not merely a footnote to it. [Q1/2026 results speech](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/events/telefonkonferenz/2026/Q1-2026%20Results%20Speech.pdf) [Q1/2026 Quarterly Statement](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2026/englisch/3-Months-Report-2026.pdf)

## FX Translation and the EUR/USD Sensitivity

AIXTRON reported in euros but generated a material portion of revenue from USD-linked contracts, so exchange rates mattered. The company used a 1.15 USD/EUR planning rate for 2024, a 1.10 rate for 2025 and a 1.20 rate for 2026 guidance. By October 2025 management was explicitly citing negative FX effects as part of the reason for narrowing full-year guidance. The exposure remained asymmetric: revenue translated lower when the dollar weakened, while much of the cost base stayed euro-denominated around Herzogenrath. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [AIXTRON Q3/2025 guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20reports%20preliminary%20Q3/2025%20results%20and%20adjusts%20FY%202025%20guidance_n13827)

chapters.title: Multi-year trajectory through GaN inflection, SiC ramp, and micro-LED reset
chapters.body:
## The Power Electronics Inflection: FY2022

AIXTRON arrived at fiscal 2022 carrying a compound-semiconductor order book reshaped by a decade of structural transition. The LED MOCVD wave had largely passed. In its place, a quieter but more durable current had begun running through demand for gallium nitride: not the blue-LED chips that once lit smartphone screens, but power transistors switching electrical current in electric-vehicle onboard chargers, data-centre power supplies, and consumer fast chargers operating at voltages where GaN's switching speed and lower conduction losses outperformed silicon.

Full-year 2022 revenue reached €463.2 million, with order intake of €585.9 million and year-end equipment backlog of €351.8 million. Those figures mattered because they showed the new cycle was not just a narrative shift: bookings were already running ahead of revenue recognition, giving management the visibility that later fed the 2023 surge. Grawert had not, as the earlier draft implied, only just become CEO in 2018; he had joined the Executive Board in August 2017 and had chaired it since 1 April 2021 after Bernd Schulte's retirement. By the 2023 annual report, AIXTRON was explicit that strong demand for MOCVD equipment for GaN and SiC power devices had been the key driver of the revenue acceleration. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2021](https://aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2021/en/Annual%20Report-2021.pdf)

The geographic composition of that demand told a story about where the GaN power supply chain was consolidating most rapidly. AIXTRON's later regional disclosures showed Asia supplying half of group revenue in 2023 and an even larger share in 2024, a pattern consistent with a China- and Asia-led first wave in wide-bandgap capacity investment. That concentration would prove both an accelerant and, later, a source of volatility. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf)

---

## Record Revenue, Rising Orders: FY2023

Fiscal 2023 represented the financial apex of AIXTRON's post-LED reconstruction. Revenue rose to €629.9 million and EBIT to €156.8 million, for an EBIT margin of 24.9%. Just as important, order intake did not decline in 2023: it increased to €640.7 million from €585.9 million in 2022, while equipment backlog ended the year at €353.7 million. The business mix showed how decisively the franchise had rotated toward power electronics, which accounted for 74% of equipment revenues, versus 12% for optoelectronics and 11% for LED including Micro LED. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf)

The qualitative story behind those numbers was equally important. AIXTRON said the year's growth was driven by strong demand for GaN and SiC power-device equipment, while the fourth quarter also saw a recovery in laser and LED demand. In other words, the 2023 earnings crest was not merely backlog conversion from an earlier order spike; it also reflected a business mix whose power franchise was maturing and whose optoelectronics line had not disappeared. That mattered because the later slowdown would be measured against a much broader base than the old LED era ever provided. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf)

The micro-LED display thesis had not yet vanished, but it was already becoming more tentative than bullish equity narratives implied. AIXTRON's own 2024 annual report would later formalise that caution by saying launches of new Micro LED products were likely to be delayed by two to three years because of technological challenges. That disclosure did not rewrite 2023's earnings story, but it changed how investors should have read the durability of the 2023 peak. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf)

---

## The SiC Adjacency

AIXTRON's G10-SiC reactor family addressed the 650-volt-and-above power market — principally EV traction inverters and other high-voltage conversion applications — where silicon carbide's wider bandgap and thermal characteristics outperformed GaN. The product was introduced in 2022, and the broader G10 family was completed in 2023 with G10-GaN and G10-AsP. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf)

SiC orders provided a second leg to the investment case, but the evidence required more discipline than the earlier draft applied. By the frozen window, the primary-source trail included Wolfspeed's April 2024 disclosure that it had placed multiple-tool orders in the second half of 2023 to support 200 mm SiC production, Nexperia's July 2024 repeat order for its 200 mm SiC volume ramp, and AIXTRON's September 2025 announcement of its 100th G10-SiC shipment to a European power-device and systems manufacturer. AIXTRON's 2025 annual report then added the competitive context: Yole estimated the company held about 27% of the SiC CVD systems market in 2024. That was credible traction, but not the same thing as uncontested leadership. [Wolfspeed selects AIXTRON tools](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Wolfspeed%20Selects%20AIXTRON%20Tools%20to%20Support%20200mm%20Production_n12560) [Nexperia order](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Nexperia%20partners%20with%20AIXTRON%20for%20200mm%20SiC%20and%20GaN%20power_n12625) [100th G10-SiC shipment](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20achieves%20100th%20G10-SiC%20Shipment%20Milestone_n13801) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

---

## Revenue Plateau and Micro LED Reset: FY2024

Fiscal 2024 confirmed the cyclical correction that order-intake trends had foreshadowed. Revenue came in at €633.2 million, order intake at €596.4 million, and EBIT at €131.2 million, leaving EBIT margin at 20.7%. The business remained profitable and far more resilient than it had been during the 2012-2014 LED collapse, but the plateau was unmistakable. AIXTRON also stepped up R&D to €91.4 million, or 14.4% of revenue, while cutting its FY2024 EBIT-margin guidance in July 2024 to 22% to 25% from 24% to 26%. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Q2/2024 guidance update](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20reports%20preliminary%20Q2/2024%20results%20with%20strong%20order%20intake.%20Momentum%20in%20SiC%20and%20GaN%20power%20continues.%20Guidance%20for%202024%20adjusted._n12621)

The most significant narrative shift of 2024 was the reset of near-term Micro LED expectations. Rather than relying on consumer-electronics reporting, AIXTRON's own annual report said the market launch of new Micro LED products was likely to be delayed by two to three years because of technological challenges. The revenue mix made the effect visible: LED including Micro LED represented 28% of equipment revenues in 2024, a level that proved unsustainable once the hoped-for launch cadence slipped. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf)

GaN power continued to generate recurring business, but velocity had moderated from the Asia-led surge of 2022-2023. That deceleration partly reflected customer-fab utilisation: tools purchased at peak had not yet been fully loaded with production volume, reducing urgency for additional capacity additions. Management's argument was that non-Chinese adoption curves in automotive, industrial and data-centre power were still moving forward, just more slowly than the first build-out wave had implied. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf)

---

## FY2025: Downcycle, Cash Recovery, and the 2026 Bridge

Entering fiscal 2025, the issue was no longer whether AIXTRON had rebuilt a real franchise; it was whether the next leg would arrive quickly enough to protect peak margins. Revenue finished the year at €556.6 million, order intake at €544.3 million and EBIT at €100.3 million. In October 2025, management cut full-year guidance after saying the demand upturn had not yet materialised in the third quarter, even as it continued to argue that medium- and long-term growth drivers in GaN and SiC remained intact. [AIXTRON FY2025 results](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20with%20robust%20results%20in%20a%20soft%20market%20environment_n13896) [AIXTRON Q3/2025 guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20reports%20preliminary%20Q3/2025%20results%20and%20adjusts%20FY%202025%20guidance_n13827)

The year was weaker on revenue and margin, but not on balance-sheet repair. Free cash flow recovered to €181.9 million from negative €72.4 million in 2024, and year-end cash rose to €224.6 million. The company used that breathing room to keep funding the 300 mm GaN program, continue SiC qualification work and prepare the next manufacturing step, including the Malaysia project later outlined in the Q1 2026 materials. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [Q1/2026 Quarterly Statement](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2026/englisch/3-Months-Report-2026.pdf)

The bridge into 2026 came not from Micro LED, and not yet from a broad-based GaN rebound, but from optoelectronics. Preliminary Q1 2026 order intake rose about 30% year-on-year to roughly €171 million, and the reported quarter closed at €171.4 million with more than 65% of equipment orders coming from optoelectronics. AIXTRON raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to around €560 million plus or minus €30 million and lifted the EBIT-margin range to 17% to 20%. That left the multi-year earnings story in a clearer frame than before: GaN power remained the core thesis, SiC was the second act, optoelectronics had become the immediate recovery driver, and Micro LED had moved back into option value rather than base-case planning. [AIXTRON guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20increases%20FY%202026%20guidance%20and%20reports%20preliminary%20Q1/2026%20figures_n13936) [Q1/2026 Quarterly Statement](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2026/englisch/3-Months-Report-2026.pdf)

chapters.title: Felix Grawert, Christian Danninger, Executive Board, Supervisory Board
chapters.body:
AIXTRON's institutional character — designing tools for adoption curves not yet visible — shaped the type of manager who eventually rose to lead it.

## Felix Grawert: An Engineer Trained on Three Continents

Felix Grawert arrived at AIXTRON in August 2017 from a career that had moved through academia, strategy consulting and industrial product management. AIXTRON's own executive-board biography listed a degree in electrical engineering from Karlsruhe, an MSc from Georgia Tech and a PhD in electrical engineering and computer science from MIT, completed in 2005. The fit with AIXTRON's later GaN and SiC emphasis was evident: before arriving in Herzogenrath, Grawert had already spent four years at Infineon running the high-voltage-conversion product line. [AIXTRON Executive Board](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/executive-board) [AIXTRON renews Felix Grawert contract](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20renews%20contract%20of%20CEO%20Dr.%20Felix%20Grawert_n13571)

From 2005 to 2013, Grawert worked as a consultant at McKinsey & Company in Munich, eventually reaching Associate Principal. His sector focus was semiconductors, high technology, and automotive — a triangulation that would prove directly applicable when GaN-on-silicon power electronics began displacing silicon MOSFETs in automotive on-board chargers and data-centre power conversion. He left McKinsey in 2013 for Infineon Technologies, where he served until 2017 as Head of Product Line High Voltage Conversion in Munich and Villach, overseeing the commercial execution of exactly the device category that AIXTRON's G10-GaN platform was designed to enable. When the AIXTRON Supervisory Board went looking for a board-level candidate who combined deep technical grounding in power semiconductors with commercial and strategic discipline, Grawert was an identifiable profile.

He joined the Executive Board in August 2017 while Bernd Schulte remained in office. The transition lasted until Schulte's retirement on 31 March 2021, after which the Supervisory Board appointed Grawert Chairman of the Executive Board effective 1 April 2021. [AIXTRON Executive Board](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/executive-board) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2021](https://aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2021/en/Annual%20Report-2021.pdf)

## The Schulte Transition and the End of a Multi-Decade Tenure

Schulte's transition culminated in 2021, not 2023. AIXTRON's 2021 annual report recorded that he retired on 31 March 2021 after nineteen years on the Executive Board, leaving Grawert to chair the board from April and Danninger to join as CFO from May. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2021](https://aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2021/en/Annual%20Report-2021.pdf)

## Christian Danninger: The Austrian CFO

Dr. Christian Danninger joined as Chief Financial Officer and Executive Board member in May 2021, filling the finance seat that had not previously existed as a standalone Vorstand position. Born in 1979 in Gmunden, Austria, Danninger brought an unusual credential set for a semiconductor equipment company: a doctorate in law from Johannes Kepler University in Linz, supplemented by dual master's degrees in law and business administration. His career had been built in industrial capital-equipment businesses — fifteen years between 2005 and 2021 split across the ENGEL Group, the Austrian plastics-injection-machinery maker, and PUTZMEISTER Holding, the German concrete-pump manufacturer where he had served as CFO from 2017. The profile — a trained lawyer-turned-capital-equipment CFO, comfortable with export-heavy manufacturing businesses and complex international customer financing — suited AIXTRON's profile as a EUR-reporting company selling long-cycle capital equipment globally. Danninger's contract runs to April 2029. [AIXTRON IR](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/executive-board)

That background also mattered to how the company navigated the 2024-2026 downturn. The quarterlies and annual reports repeatedly cast Danninger less as a promotional markets figure than as the steward of working capital, FX assumptions, cash rebuilding and the financing flexibility that later included the April 2026 convertible bond. In a business where one or two delayed tool deliveries can distort a quarter, that style of CFO mattered as much as headline guidance. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [Q1/2026 Quarterly Statement](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2026/englisch/3-Months-Report-2026.pdf)

## The Linck Interlude and a Lean Two-Person Board

The third Executive Board member appointed in 2021, Dr. Jochen Linck, served as Chief Operating Officer with responsibility for R&D and operations — procurement, manufacturing, logistics, quality, and IT. Linck's departure in September 2023, which the company disclosed in May of that year as a decision not to renew his contract for personal reasons, reduced the Vorstand back to two members. Rather than appointing a successor to the COO seat, AIXTRON created an internal Executive Committee — a layer of senior vice presidents covering the former COO portfolio — that reports directly to Grawert and Danninger. The structure has been characterised internally as a deliberate move toward operating flexibility, concentrating formal accountability at the top while distributing functional depth below board level. [AIXTRON press release, May 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20introduces%20new%20Executive%20Committee%20/%20Current%20COO%20Jochen%20Linck%20not%20to%20renew%20his%20contract%20due%20to%20personal%20reasons%20/%20New%20Executive%20Committee%20will%20support%20CEO%20and%20CFO_n2443)

The Supervisory Board's decision in September 2024 to extend Grawert's contract by a further five years — through 13 August 2030 — reflected a verdict on his first three years as chairman. In AIXTRON's own release, then-chairman Kim Schindelhauer said Grawert had driven significant progress in power electronics and optoelectronics, while Grawert said the next phase would focus on expanding technological leadership. [AIXTRON renews Felix Grawert contract](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20renews%20contract%20of%20CEO%20Dr.%20Felix%20Grawert_n13571)

## Grawert's Strategic Voice

On earnings calls, Grawert tended toward declarative technical-commercial framing rather than promotional tone. Through the soft 2025 period and into the April 2026 guidance raise, his public messaging kept returning to the same structure: weak near-term GaN and SiC demand, a stronger optoelectronics surprise, and a longer-term conviction that AI data-centre power architectures would still support wide-bandgap adoption. [AIXTRON Q3/2025 guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20reports%20preliminary%20Q3/2025%20results%20and%20adjusts%20FY%202025%20guidance_n13827) [AIXTRON FY2025 results](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20with%20robust%20results%20in%20a%20soft%20market%20environment_n13896) [AIXTRON guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20increases%20FY%202026%20guidance%20and%20reports%20preliminary%20Q1/2026%20figures_n13936)

> "The demand upturn has not yet materialized in Q3/2025..." — Felix Grawert, 17 October 2025 [AIXTRON Q3/2025 guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20reports%20preliminary%20Q3/2025%20results%20and%20adjusts%20FY%202025%20guidance_n13827)

The point was less the phrasing than the consistency. Even after cutting guidance in October 2025, management still described the medium- and long-term growth drivers in GaN, SiC and Micro LED as intact; by April 2026, the company was using a stronger optoelectronics order book to raise guidance while still calling GaN stable but soft and SiC weak. Whether the cycle had truly turned by 23 May 2026 is addressed elsewhere in the dossier; the narrower point here is that Grawert did not walk back the end-market thesis through the down-cycle. [AIXTRON Q3/2025 guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20reports%20preliminary%20Q3/2025%20results%20and%20adjusts%20FY%202025%20guidance_n13827) [AIXTRON guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20increases%20FY%202026%20guidance%20and%20reports%20preliminary%20Q1/2026%20figures_n13936)

## The Supervisory Board: Industry Credentials Rebuilt Around Semiconductors

Germany's two-tier governance model places the Aufsichtsrat — Supervisory Board — in a constitutionally distinct oversight role from the operating Vorstand. AIXTRON's six-member Supervisory Board, as constituted by the 2025 annual general meeting, has been substantially refreshed since the post-LED-cycle restructuring years.

The most consequential recent change was the election of Alexander Everke as chairman following Kim Schindelhauer's resignation at the 2025 AGM. AIXTRON's own governance disclosures show Everke's semiconductor lineage clearly enough without embellishment: Siemens, Infineon, NXP and ams/ams-OSRAM before joining AIXTRON's Supervisory Board in 2024 and becoming its chairman in 2025. He also chaired the Capital Markets and Nomination committees. [AIXTRON Supervisory Board](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/supervisory-board) [AIXTRON AGM 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20Annual%20General%20Meeting%202025%20-%20All%20resolutions%20approved%20by%20a%20large%20majority._n13716) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

Deputy chairman Frits van Hout, on the board since 2019, brought the complementary perspective of a long ASML career and chaired the Remuneration Committee. [AIXTRON Supervisory Board](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/supervisory-board) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

The remaining members spanned audit, technology operations and capital-markets expertise. Ingo Bank joined in 2025; Karen Florschutz and Alexander Everke had been elected in 2024; Stefan Traeger had served since 2022; and Prof. Dr. Anna Weber, on the board since 2019, chaired the Audit Committee. Those dates and committee roles were set out in AIXTRON's 2025 governance statement rather than in secondary reporting. [AIXTRON Supervisory Board](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/supervisory-board) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

| Member | Role | Board since | Background anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alexander Everke | Chairman | 2024 | Semiconductor executive across Infineon, NXP and ams/ams-OSRAM |
| Frits van Hout | Deputy Chairman | 2019 | Former ASML executive |
| Ingo Bank | Member | 2025 | CFO City Football Group; former CFO at ams-OSRAM and OSRAM |
| Karen Florschütz | Member | 2024 | Executive vice president at Airbus Defence and Space |
| Dr. Stefan Traeger | Member | 2022 | CEO of JENOPTIK AG |
| Prof. Dr. Anna Weber | Member (Audit chair) | 2019 | Academic specialist in accounting and auditing |

The concentration of ams-OSRAM alumni — Everke and Bank both served there, as CFO and CEO respectively — at the top of the Supervisory Board in 2025 was the most visible signal of where the board believed AIXTRON's strategic reference points lay: not in legacy LED equipment or generic industrial capital equipment, but in the compound-semiconductor photonics and power-electronics complex that connects MOCVD deposition to AI infrastructure, automotive electrification, and optical datacom. Whether that strategic alignment translates into order-book execution over the remainder of the decade is the question Grawert and Danninger are contracted to answer.

The 2025 AGM and governance statement also made clear that this was no symbolic board refresh. Everke chaired the Supervisory Board while van Hout led remuneration, Weber audit, and Everke himself chaired the Capital Markets and Nomination committees. For investors reading AIXTRON through a German governance lens, that committee architecture mattered because it concentrated semiconductor experience not just in biography lines but in the parts of the board most directly linked to succession, capital allocation and market communication. [AIXTRON AGM 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20Annual%20General%20Meeting%202025%20-%20All%20resolutions%20approved%20by%20a%20large%20majority._n13716) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) That level of committee detail rarely changes the investment case on its own, but in AIXTRON's case it reinforced how deliberately the board had been reassembled around semiconductor and photonics experience.

chapters.title: Power, photonics, and display device-maker customers plus the Herzogenrath manufacturing footprint
chapters.body:
AIXTRON's customers sorted into four clusters: GaN power electronics (the core), SiC power devices (contested), photonics (steady), and micro-LED display (thesis unconfirmed).

## GaN Power Electronics: The Core Customer Bloc

The anchoring customers for AIXTRON's GaN and SiC platforms spanned European integrated device manufacturers and a fast-expanding Asian ecosystem, but the company's own disclosures became more concrete around named accounts only in selected cases. The cleanest disclosed examples around the frozen window were Nexperia, which said in July 2024 it was using AIXTRON for both 200 mm SiC and GaN power ramps, and Renesas, which in May 2026 took multiple Planetary G5+C systems for high-volume GaN manufacturing expansion. Those releases tied AIXTRON's power franchise directly to data-centre, automotive, renewable-energy and industrial power-conversion applications. [Nexperia order](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Nexperia%20partners%20with%20AIXTRON%20for%20200mm%20SiC%20and%20GaN%20power_n12625) [Renesas order](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20supplied%20Planetary%20GaN%20MOCVD%20Systems%20to%20Renesas%20for%20High-Volume%20Manufacturing%20Expansion_n13970)

The second layer of the customer map sat one step removed from AIXTRON itself: fabless GaN and photonics designers depended on wafer suppliers and device makers that owned the epitaxy tools. That structure meant AIXTRON's customer evidence often surfaced in equipment orders disclosed by named IDMs and foundries rather than in a complete public customer roster. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

The most consequential new GaN customer geography, however, was China. Innoscience, a Zhuhai-based GaN-on-Si manufacturer that had previously publicised its use of AIXTRON tools, illustrated the sort of capacity expansion that sat behind the company's Asia-heavy mix, even though AIXTRON did not publish a complete account-by-account customer roster for the 2022-2026 period. China's broader policy emphasis on domestic semiconductor self-sufficiency gave a structural tailwind to this activity that showed little sign of abating through the frozen snapshot window, even as export-control scrutiny across the wider semiconductor supply chain intensified. [Innoscience press release](https://www.aixtron.com/presse/2018/2018-11/181121%20Innoscience_e_final.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

AIXTRON's annual report and investor communications confirmed that power electronics — principally GaN — had become the single largest revenue contributor in the equipment mix by the mid-2020s, having displaced LED MOCVD tools as the dominant product line during the prior cycle.

## SiC Power Epitaxy: Entering a Contested Landscape

The G10-SiC platform, commercialised through 2023–2024, brought AIXTRON into direct competition with established SiC epi-tool suppliers including Veeco Instruments, as well as with purpose-built SiC specialists that had historically dominated silicon-carbide homoepitaxial growth. The SiC power device market itself was expanding rapidly, driven by EV traction inverter adoption — Tesla, BYD, and the European automotive OEM supply chains had collectively pulled forward enormous SiC demand — and Wolfspeed, the Cree spin-off, stood as the most prominent customer archetype: a vertically integrated SiC device maker racing to bring its Siler City, North Carolina mega-fab into full production.

The public record on SiC was firmer than the draft implied. Nexperia explicitly disclosed a repeat G10-SiC order in July 2024 for its 200 mm SiC volume ramp, and AIXTRON said in September 2025 that its 100th G10-SiC shipment had gone to a European power-device and systems manufacturer supporting 200 mm production. Beyond those disclosed wins, management still described the market largely through qualification progress, utilisation trends and market-share positioning rather than a full named-customer list. [Nexperia order](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Nexperia%20partners%20with%20AIXTRON%20for%20200mm%20SiC%20and%20GaN%20power_n12625) [100th G10-SiC shipment](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20achieves%20100th%20G10-SiC%20Shipment%20Milestone_n13801) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## Photonics: Datacom Lasers, VCSELs, and Tier-1 Optical Supply Chains

AIXTRON's GaAs and InP MOCVD platforms continued to serve the photonics supply chain with equipment for laser diodes, VCSELs and photonic integrated circuits. Here the disclosed customer trail was unusually direct: Nokia ordered a G10-AsP system in April 2025 for 6-inch InP photonics, and Lumentum placed multiple G10-AsP orders in May 2026 for AI-network optical connectivity. The Q3 2025 transcript also said the G10-AsP was establishing itself as the tool of record to the laser market. [Nokia order](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20delivers%20G10-AsP%20for%20production%20of%20next%20generation%20photonics%20to%20Nokia_n13685) [Lumentum order](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20receives%20multiple%20orders%20for%20G10-AsP%20MOCVD%20Systems%20from%20Lumentum%20to%20support%20expansion%20of%20High-Speed%20Optical%20Solutions%20for%20AI%20Networks_n13987) [Q3 2025 transcript](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/events/telefonkonferenz/2025/AIXTRON_SE_Q3_2025_transcript.pdf)

The VCSEL sub-segment still mattered because it linked AIXTRON to 3D sensing, automotive and short-reach optical markets, but the cleaner primary-source trail ran through named device makers rather than through consumer OEM inference. AIXTRON's disclosed photonics orders around Nokia and Lumentum were therefore more defensible anchors than speculation around handset programmes. [Nokia order](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20delivers%20G10-AsP%20for%20production%20of%20next%20generation%20photonics%20to%20Nokia_n13685) [Lumentum order](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20receives%20multiple%20orders%20for%20G10-AsP%20MOCVD%20Systems%20from%20Lumentum%20to%20support%20expansion%20of%20High-Speed%20Optical%20Solutions%20for%20AI%20Networks_n13987)

Automotive LiDAR added a second photonics growth vector. The expansion of production-intent LiDAR systems across the automotive OEM supply chain — through suppliers including Luminar, Innoviz, and Valeo — drove demand for pulsed-laser-diode and VCSEL capacity that fed back to the same tier-1 photonics device makers running AIXTRON tools.

## Micro-LED Display: The Thesis That Stalled

Micro-LED display generated substantial investor discussion but delivered minimal confirmed production-scale revenue. AIXTRON's own 2024 annual report said new Micro LED launches were likely to be delayed by two to three years, and the 2025 revenue mix showed LED including Micro LED falling to 15% of systems sales. Research tools and pilot-line equipment were in the field, but mass-production capacity orders had not materialised by the frozen date. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## Geographic Mix and Export-Control Exposure

AIXTRON's revenue has historically carried a pronounced Asian weighting, with China, Taiwan, South Korea, and Japan collectively accounting for the majority of equipment deliveries in most fiscal years. China alone, at peak LED MOCVD cycle volumes in the 2010s, exceeded half of group revenue in certain periods. Through the GaN power cycle of 2022–2024, China remained the single largest country revenue contributor — driven by Innoscience and the broader domestic GaN foundry buildout — though the proportional share moderated as European and North American GaN capacity orders grew.

| Region | Principal customer types | Demand driver |
|--------|--------------------------|---------------|
| China | GaN foundries and power-device manufacturers | Domestic semi policy, consumer and industrial power |
| Taiwan | Display and photonics manufacturers | Micro-LED pilots, VCSEL and PIC work |
| South Korea | Display and advanced-material customers | Micro-LED R&D and pilot lines |
| Japan | Photonics and power-device producers | Datacom, automotive LiDAR and power conversion |
| North America | SiC, GaN and photonics manufacturers | EV, data-centre and optical infrastructure |
| Europe | Automotive and industrial power-device makers | Automotive, industrial and energy applications |

This China exposure drew sustained attention from AIXTRON's investor base and from German and European regulators. MOCVD equipment did not fall, through the snapshot date, within the most tightly controlled categories of the U.S. Commerce Department's Export Administration Regulations as applied to advanced logic and memory fabs. But compound-semiconductor epi tools occupy a grey zone in dual-use export control frameworks. AIXTRON applied for and received export licences on a transaction-by-transaction basis for sensitive end-users, disclosing compliance costs without quantifying lost-order exposure from licence denials.
