The October 2023 and subsequent expansions of U.S. advanced-chip export controls created a durable overhang: AIXTRON's GaN and SiC tools served power and photonics applications that remained outside the most stringent controls as of the snapshot date, but the regulatory trajectory pointed toward progressive tightening. Any future extension of compound-semiconductor controls into the GaN power device supply chain would directly affect Innoscience and comparable Chinese foundry customers.

## The Herzogenrath Footprint

AIXTRON operates a capital-light, design-and-assemble model from Herzogenrath. Critical components — quartz and ceramic reactor parts, gas delivery systems, vacuum hardware — are sourced from a global tier-one supplier base. The company expanded cleanroom test and assembly capacity during the 2022–2024 GaN power ramp. The official facility list in the 2025 annual report put the supporting footprint in Cambridge in the UK, Turin, Heerlen, Santa Clara, Hwaseong, Shanghai, Hsinchu, Tokyo and Kulim. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

chapters.title: Where AIXTRON sits against Veeco plus the broader MOCVD and compound-semi equipment set
chapters.body:
## The Duopoly That Survived the LED Bust

The global MOCVD market did not remain a literal two-company monopoly after the LED bust, but it did remain heavily concentrated at the high end. In AIXTRON's own 2025 annual report, Yole estimated that the company held 77% of the global compound-semiconductor MOCVD market in 2024, with Veeco at 8%, Taiyo Nippon Sanso at 5% and AMEC at 4%. That was a more precise and more defensible formulation than the earlier draft's rough 80-90% duopoly claim: the market had broadened, yet AIXTRON and Veeco still defined the Western competitive frame. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## The Veeco Rivalry: From LED Wars to Power Electronics

Veeco Instruments, headquartered in Plainview, New York, remained AIXTRON's most direct Western competitor. Both companies had lived through the LED boom and its correction, but their responses diverged. Veeco broadened itself with the Ultratech acquisition announced in 2017 at about $815 million and later bought Epiluvac in 2023 to accelerate its move into SiC epitaxy. AIXTRON stayed more concentrated around compound-semiconductor deposition. The distinction mattered because it shaped how each company could fund R&D through down-cycles: Veeco from a broader portfolio, AIXTRON from tighter specialisation. [Veeco-Ultratech announcement](https://ir.veeco.com/news-and-events/news-details/2017/Veeco-Enters-into-Agreement-to-Acquire-Ultratech/default.aspx) [Veeco-Epiluvac announcement](https://ir.veeco.com/news-and-events/news-details/2023/Veeco-Acquires-Epiluvac-AB-to-Accelerate-Penetration-Into--High-Growth-Silicon-Carbide-Epitaxy-Equipment-Market/default.aspx)

## Platform Comparison: G10-GaN versus Western Rivals

The sharpest competitive battleground through 2024-2026 remained GaN-on-Si epitaxy for power-electronics applications — the transistors and diodes going into data-centre power supplies, electric-vehicle chargers and consumer adapters. AIXTRON's answer was the G10-GaN, which its annual reports described as a fully automated, compact MOCVD cluster tool for 150 mm and 200 mm high-production factories. The company simultaneously kept pointing to the 300 mm transition as the next technological step, with the Herzogenrath Innovation Center built to support that move. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

The architectural point mattered because AIXTRON's competitive story was not merely that it sold a tool, but that it had process history across a very large installed base. Veeco pitched a different engineering approach and broader process portfolio; AIXTRON kept leaning into cost of ownership, process transfer, automation and customer familiarity. The practical result was not a clean geographic split, but a market in which AIXTRON still looked strongest where customers wanted mature high-volume GaN manufacturing and where a pre-existing installed base reduced qualification friction.

| Feature | AIXTRON | Key disclosed rival reference |
|---|---|---|
| GaN power platform | G10-GaN, 150/200 mm compact MOCVD cluster tool; 300 mm transition under development | Veeco GaN MOCVD portfolio |
| SiC platform | G10-SiC, 9x150 mm / 6x200 mm dual-size batch reactor | ASM/LPE, Tokyo Electron, Veeco |
| Photonics platform | G10-AsP and G5 family | Specialist photonics MOCVD peers |
| Company-stated edge | Process transfer, automation, cost of ownership, installed base | Rival process architectures and broader tool portfolios |

For SiC epitaxy — a newer battleground as the power-device industry expanded SiC adoption for EV inverters and industrial drives — the rivalry widened beyond Veeco. AIXTRON's 2025 annual report said Yole estimated its 2024 SiC CVD market share at about 27%, versus 32% for ASM and 16% for Tokyo Electron. ASM had strengthened its position with the agreed acquisition of LPE in 2022, while AIXTRON was still building share through disclosed wins such as Wolfspeed's 2024 tool selection, Nexperia's repeat order and the 100th G10-SiC shipment in September 2025. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [ASM-LPE announcement](https://www.asm.com/press-releases/asm-announces-agreement-to-acquire-lpe-entering-high-growth-silicon-carbide-epitaxy-equipment-business-2480778) [Wolfspeed selects AIXTRON tools](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Wolfspeed%20Selects%20AIXTRON%20Tools%20to%20Support%20200mm%20Production_n12560) [Nexperia order](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Nexperia%20partners%20with%20AIXTRON%20for%20200mm%20SiC%20and%20GaN%20power_n12625) [100th G10-SiC shipment](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20achieves%20100th%20G10-SiC%20Shipment%20Milestone_n13801)

## Chinese MOCVD: A Contained but Funded Threat

The most visible competitive shift of the post-LED decade was the rise of Chinese domestic equipment makers. AIXTRON's own 2025 market-share disclosure still showed AMEC at only 4% of the global compound-semiconductor MOCVD market, which suggested that the power-grade and photonics-grade franchise remained difficult to dislodge quickly. But the strategic risk was not today's percentage so much as the persistence of policy support. AIXTRON's risk disclosures repeatedly paired Chinese localisation pressure with export-control friction, effectively acknowledging that even where domestic tools lagged on process performance, state policy could still narrow the accessible market over time. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

What Chinese equipment makers had already achieved, however, was to turn price and localisation into a durable competitive vector. For AIXTRON, that meant the margin of safety lay less in headline market share than in maintaining a material process-performance lead in defect density, throughput and repeatability at the applications that customers could not afford to qualify twice.

## Photonics: Niche Depth as a Defensive Moat

In photonics-grade MOCVD — InP-based laser diodes for datacom transceivers, GaAs VCSELs for 3D sensing, and photonic integrated-circuit structures — AIXTRON occupied territory where the competitive set narrowed considerably. Here the company's own disclosures were stronger than the draft's generic customer lists: the Q3 2025 transcript said the G10-AsP was establishing itself as the tool of record to the laser market, Nokia ordered a G10-AsP system in April 2025, and Lumentum placed multiple G10-AsP orders in May 2026 to support AI-network optical connectivity. [Q3 2025 transcript](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/events/telefonkonferenz/2025/AIXTRON_SE_Q3_2025_transcript.pdf) [Nokia order](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20delivers%20G10-AsP%20for%20production%20of%20next%20generation%20photonics%20to%20Nokia_n13685) [Lumentum order](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20receives%20multiple%20orders%20for%20G10-AsP%20MOCVD%20Systems%20from%20Lumentum%20to%20support%20expansion%20of%20High-Speed%20Optical%20Solutions%20for%20AI%20Networks_n13987)

The photonics segment mattered strategically because it provided revenue diversity that did not run on exactly the same timing as GaN or SiC power capex. Optical interconnect demand tied to AI infrastructure gave AIXTRON an end-market vector that was less dependent on EV production schedules or the inventory digestion of power-device customers.

## Strategic Position: Structural Advantages and Exposed Flanks

AIXTRON's competitive position at the frozen date rested on several structural advantages unlikely to erode quickly: a still-dominant disclosed share in overall compound-semiconductor MOCVD, a broad product family spanning GaN, SiC and photonics, and an installed base large enough to generate follow-on service and process-stickiness benefits. The company's engineering depth across multiple material systems remained a real moat, especially where customers were optimizing multi-step production lines and were reluctant to reopen qualification risk.

The vulnerabilities were equally legible. SiC remained a share-building contest rather than a won market. Micro LED had moved out in time after AIXTRON itself said commercial launches were delayed by two to three years. And Chinese localisation, amplified by export-control regimes, threatened to erode the edges of the Asia opportunity even if the tools themselves remained technically strong. The duopoly that emerged from the LED era survived into the power-electronics transition, but it now operated on more segmented and more application-specific terrain than the old uniform LED capex cycle ever provided.

One additional buffer deserves emphasis: the installed base itself. By 2025 AIXTRON was generating €112.0 million of service, spare-parts and related revenue, evidence that competitive position was no longer expressed only in new-tool market share but also in the recurring economics of tools already qualified in customer fabs. That recurring layer did not remove the capex cycle, but it did raise the cost for rivals trying to displace the incumbent one process module at a time. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) It also meant that competitive slippage would probably show up first in new order share and only later in the installed-base annuity, giving close readers of order intake an early warning system.

chapters.title: Timeline from 1983 founding through GaN power inflection and micro-LED reset
chapters.body:
## From the Aachen Laboratory to the Public Market

AIXTRON's own history page said the company was founded in 1983 by employees of RWTH Aachen's Institute for Semiconductor Technology. The same chronology recorded its IPO in 1997, not 1998. By the 2025 annual report the shares were trading in Frankfurt's Prime Standard and were constituents of both MDAX and TecDAX. [AIXTRON History](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/about-aixtron/history) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## The LED Cycle: Boom, Bust, and Strategic Reset

The LED cycle remained the defining commercial event of AIXTRON's first thirty years. The 2011 annual report showed revenues of €783.8 million in 2010 and €611.0 million in 2011 before the market correction bit hard. That bust set the context for everything that followed: tighter portfolio discipline, less dependence on a single application and a harder look at China-related concentration. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2011](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2011/en/Annual%20Report%202011.pdf)

## The 2016 Interruption: Chinese Bid and the Forced Pivot

In 2016, Grand Chip Investment GmbH, backed by Fujian Grand Chip Investment Fund LP, launched its takeover attempt for AIXTRON. The sequence that mattered was two-step: Germany withdrew its clearance certificate on 24 October 2016, and the U.S. President blocked the acquisition of AIXTRON's U.S. business on 3 December 2016. The failed bid reinforced the strategic value of AIXTRON's technology base just as the company was searching for its next cycle. [AIXTRON, 24 October 2016](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20Withdrawal%20of%20Clearance%20Certificate%20and%20reopening%20of%20review%20proceedings%20by%20the%20Ministry%20of%20Economics%20pertaining%20to%20the%20takeover%20by%20Grand%20Chip%20Investment%20GmbH_n894) [AIXTRON, 3 December 2016](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/AIXTRON%20SE%20Tender%20Offer%20by%20Grand%20Chip%20Investment%20GmbH%20/%20Prohibition%20of%20Acquisition%20of%20U.S.%20Business%20of%20AIXTRON%20by%20the%20U.S.%20President_n892)

## The Grawert Era: Repositioning the Product Portfolio

Grawert joined the Executive Board in August 2017, became chairman on 1 April 2021 after Bernd Schulte's retirement, and then oversaw the completion of the G10 family: G10-SiC in 2022, followed by G10-GaN and G10-AsP in 2023. That was the operational expression of the strategic reset toward GaN power electronics, SiC epitaxy and photonics. [AIXTRON Executive Board](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/executive-board) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2021](https://aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2021/en/Annual%20Report-2021.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf)

## SiC Entry, Micro LED Delay, Opto Upswing

The key catalyst sequence through the frozen window was not one event but three. First, AIXTRON disclosed concrete SiC wins, including Nexperia's 2024 repeat order and the 100th G10-SiC shipment in 2025. Second, the company said in its 2024 annual report that Micro LED launches had slipped by two to three years, resetting the display timetable. Third, Q1 2026 optoelectronics orders came in far stronger than expected, prompting a guidance raise. [Nexperia order](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/finance-news/Nexperia%20partners%20with%20AIXTRON%20for%20200mm%20SiC%20and%20GaN%20power_n12625) [100th G10-SiC shipment](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20achieves%20100th%20G10-SiC%20Shipment%20Milestone_n13801) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20increases%20FY%202026%20guidance%20and%20reports%20preliminary%20Q1/2026%20figures_n13936)

## Forward Catalysts Through the 2026 Horizon

By the frozen snapshot date, the near-term catalyst map had narrowed to a more disciplined set of variables: recovery timing in GaN power, utilisation and qualification progress in SiC, and the durability of the optoelectronics order surprise. The 2026 guidance raise made clear which of those was moving first: photonics, not display, had become the immediate positive swing factor. [Q1/2026 Quarterly Statement](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2026/englisch/3-Months-Report-2026.pdf) [AIXTRON guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20increases%20FY%202026%20guidance%20and%20reports%20preliminary%20Q1/2026%20figures_n13936)

chapters.title: MOCVD reactor IP, compound-semi process technology, R&D framework
chapters.body:
## Planetary Reactors and the Aachen Inheritance

AIXTRON's intellectual identity was forged on a conviction: compound-semiconductor thin-film deposition required fundamentally better reactor geometry, not merely better chemistry.

The core of AIXTRON's IP estate is the **Planetary Reactor** concept — a design in which individual wafer carriers, called satellites, rotate on their own axes while simultaneously orbiting a central axis on a large rotating susceptor. The compound motion is not decorative engineering; it is the mechanism that exposes each wafer to the same time-averaged gas composition and thermal environment. In metal-organic chemical vapor deposition, where epitaxial layer thicknesses are measured in nanometres and dopant concentrations must be controlled to parts per billion, uniformity is not a specification category but a yield-determining variable. AIXTRON's patent filings, accumulated across four decades, reflect an obsessive refinement of this central geometry — satellite design, gas-foil rotation (which allows wafers to float on a thin cushion of process gas, reducing particle generation), susceptor materials, and the thermal boundary conditions that govern growth kinetics.

Alongside the Planetary Reactor family, AIXTRON developed the **Close Coupled Showerhead (CCS)** architecture, used in its AIX 2600 G5 platform and adapted for several optoelectronic applications. In the CCS design, the gas distribution plate sits in close proximity to the wafer surface, minimising the mixing length and enabling sharper compositional transitions between epitaxial layers — critical for heterojunction structures in laser diodes, VCSELs, and high-electron-mobility transistors. The two architectures — planetary susceptor and close-coupled showerhead — constitute a product bifurcation that lets AIXTRON address different substrate sizes, chemistries, and wafer-count economics across its tool catalogue.

## Process IP Across Material Systems

Each compound-semiconductor material system presents its own set of thermodynamic and chemical obstacles, and AIXTRON's process IP is stratified accordingly.

For **GaN-on-Si** power devices, the central challenge was the substantial thermal-expansion mismatch between gallium nitride and silicon. AIXTRON's public technology material described its answer in process-control rather than marketing terms: wafer-level temperature control, particle reduction and reproducible uniformity across 150 mm and 200 mm wafers. In practice that meant the company was selling process know-how alongside the hardware, not merely the chamber itself. [G10-GaN](https://www.aixtron.com/en/products/G10-GaN_p2739) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

For **SiC homoepitaxy**, the physics are different in kind. Silicon carbide grows at temperatures above 1,500°C — roughly twice the growth temperature for GaN — and the chemistry involves chlorinated precursors that are corrosive to conventional reactor components. The G10-SiC platform, commercialised by 2023, required AIXTRON to develop susceptor materials, liner designs, and gas injection systems tolerant of those conditions. The IP around high-temperature SiC epitaxy thus extends into materials science — specifically the development of graphite and silicon carbide–coated components that maintain dimensional stability and do not introduce metallic contamination into the epi layer.

For **GaAs and InP** optoelectronic devices — laser diodes for datacom transceivers, automotive LiDAR chips, VCSELs for 3D sensing — AIXTRON's process IP centres on phosphorus handling (white phosphorus is pyrophoric and requires careful abatement), ultra-thin quantum well accuracy, and the multi-layer arsenide/phosphide structures that define device bandgap engineering. The CCS platform has been the primary vehicle for these applications, and the process knowledge embedded in tool configurations represents years of co-development with customers such as II-VI/Coherent and Lumentum.

## The Aachen Research Ecosystem

Research collaborations with Fraunhofer institutes sat alongside a physical R&D footprint concentrated in Herzogenrath. The company history page showed that the Thomas Swan Scientific Equipment division was acquired in 1999, not 2002, and the 2025 annual report listed Cambridge as the relevant UK site together with Santa Clara and several Asian service locations. By 2025, R&D expenditure had risen to €81.1 million, or roughly 15% of revenue. [AIXTRON History](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/about-aixtron/history) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## Patent Portfolio and Competitive Moat

AIXTRON's patent estate spans reactor geometry, gas distribution hardware, susceptor and satellite designs, thermal management systems, in-situ measurement methods and process sequences for specific material systems. The company had in fact disclosed the aggregate count: the group held 306 patent families as of 31 December 2025, up from 295 at the end of 2024 and 265 at the end of 2023. That did not make any single patent dispositive, but it did show a steadily refreshed portfolio layered over four decades of process engineering. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf)

Veeco Instruments, AIXTRON's principal competitor in MOCVD for power and photonics applications, pursues broadly similar deposition physics through different mechanical implementations — most notably its TurboDisc platform, which uses a different rotation geometry. The existence of two viable MOCVD architectures has prevented either company from achieving absolute monopoly, but AIXTRON's Planetary Reactor remains the dominant tool in GaN power production lines at the customers that have publicly disclosed their equipment choices. The R&D moat was also being renewed physically: the Herzogenrath Innovation Center was built to support the transition to 300 mm technology, making the patent base relevant not only to legacy platforms but to the next wafer-size step as well. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

The institutional memory encoded in AIXTRON's engineering organisation — the accumulated heuristics of growing compound semiconductors in production for four decades — may ultimately be more durable than any individual patent filing. That memory, rooted in the Aachen academic tradition and refined through thousands of customer process interactions, is the company's deepest competitive asset.

chapters.title: Capital-cycle cyclicality, China export controls, micro-LED uncertainty, FX, competitive, governance
chapters.body:
## The Capital Cycle's Long Shadow

The GaN and SiC power inflection that drove AIXTRON to €629.9 million in fiscal 2023 revenue bore the same structural signature as the LED super-cycle: customers ordered in clusters, then entered a digestion phase. By 2024, portions of the customer base were pausing new orders while running installed tools toward fuller utilisation. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2023/en/Annual-Report-2023.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf)

The structural risk is the asymmetry of the order signal. A customer commissioning a new SiC fab may spend twelve months ordering and receiving tools, then run those tools for three to five years before ordering incremental capacity. AIXTRON's backlog and order intake—disclosed quarterly—are therefore coincident indicators of customer capital commitment rather than leading indicators of end-market demand. Even sustained GaN adoption growth can coexist with multi-quarter equipment order softness, and the market's valuation of AIXTRON tends to punish that softness harshly at the first sign of deceleration.

## China: The Licence Overhang

China has been among AIXTRON's most consequential customer geographies across multiple product cycles, from the LED MOCVD era through the more recent GaN and SiC power device buildout. In recent fiscal years, Chinese-sourced revenue represented a meaningful double-digit share of total group revenue—a concentration that became increasingly fraught as Western governments moved to constrain China's advanced semiconductor manufacturing capability.

From 2023 onward, German authorities, operating under the EU dual-use export control framework, required individual export licences for certain AIXTRON MOCVD tool shipments to China. The scope of the licensing requirement, the category of Chinese customers deemed eligible to receive equipment, and the timeline for licence approvals introduced an overhang on near-term China order conversion that AIXTRON could not resolve through commercial negotiation alone. The company's quarterly order disclosures were, in effect, a running scorecard of the licensing environment as well as underlying customer demand. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

The deeper structural risk was not administrative but competitive. AMEC and Naura, both listed Chinese equipment makers with access to state-adjacent capital, have been investing systematically to develop domestic MOCVD capability for power electronics and photonics applications. Their near-term process performance lagged AIXTRON's G10 platform metrics on wafer uniformity and throughput — specifications that demanding GaN and SiC power-device customers benchmark rigorously — but the gap was narrowing. A China that sources more MOCVD equipment domestically represents not a temporary headwind but a permanent reduction in the addressable market for AIXTRON's China revenue. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## The Micro-LED Thesis Deferred

AIXTRON's own disclosure was more disciplined than the earlier draft's consumer-OEM attribution. The 2024 annual report said launches for new Micro LEDs were likely to be delayed by two to three years because of technological challenges, and the 2025 mix data showed LED including Micro LED falling sharply as a share of systems revenue. Each year of deferral gave OLED, mini-LED and other incumbent display technologies more time to entrench themselves. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## Currency: Structural Translation Drag

AIXTRON's financial architecture creates a persistent asymmetry between where it earns and where it spends. The company reports in euros; its cost base—engineering staff, manufacturing, and administration in Herzogenrath and the Aachen corridor—is predominantly euro-denominated. Its revenue, by contrast, flows from customers in the United States, China, Korea, Japan, Taiwan, and across Southeast Asia, where billing currencies include US dollars, renminbi, won, and yen.

Euro appreciation against those billing currencies compressed reported revenue and margin without any underlying change in tool volume. AIXTRON could hedge near-term transaction exposure, but not the broader translation effect that came from selling globally while keeping much of its engineering and manufacturing cost base in Germany. The company's own guidance history captured the point: it planned around 1.15 USD/EUR for 2024, 1.10 for 2025 and 1.20 for 2026, and by October 2025 it was explicitly citing negative FX effects in its guidance cut. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf) [AIXTRON Q3/2025 guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/investors/news/AIXTRON%20reports%20preliminary%20Q3/2025%20results%20and%20adjusts%20FY%202025%20guidance_n13827)

## Competitive Intensity: East and West

AIXTRON's MOCVD franchise is the dominant European position in its niche, but competition from two directions was intensifying through the frozen window.

| Competitor | Geography | Relevant platform | Competitive vector |
|---|---|---|---|
| Veeco Instruments | USA | Propel (GaN power MOCVD) | US customer relationships; ITAR/supply-chain-risk framing for domestic defence/power buyers |
| AMEC | China | Domestic GaN / compound-semi tools | China market localisation; state-supported pricing |
| Naura Technology | China | Compound-semi epi equipment | Vertically integrated Chinese fab customer relationships |

Veeco represents the most direct process-performance competition in the near term. Its Propel platform targets the same GaN-on-Si and GaN-on-SiC power device applications as AIXTRON's G10-GaN tool, and its US domicile is a commercial advantage in procurement decisions influenced by supply-chain sovereignty considerations—including US defence and data-centre customers who may favour domestic equipment vendors. Veeco's scale, however, remained smaller than AIXTRON's through the frozen window, limiting its ability to match AIXTRON's installed-base density and customer intimacy in the field.

The AMEC and Naura vector is a longer-horizon risk with potentially larger magnitude. Both companies benefited from the Chinese government's explicit equipment self-sufficiency programme, accessing capital at terms that Western capital markets would not replicate. Their strategy—first to capture domestic Chinese customers with good-enough tools at lower cost, then to expand into third-country markets—tracked the historical trajectory of other Chinese equipment categories. AIXTRON's competitive moat in this scenario depends on maintaining a durable process-performance lead: if its tool platforms run GaN or SiC device epitaxy at meaningfully higher yields or throughput than Chinese alternatives, domestic substitution is slow. If that gap narrows faster than expected, the margin at which AIXTRON can price globally compresses.

## Governance and Capital-Market Volatility

The factual issue was index placement: AIXTRON's own 2025 annual report said the shares were constituents of MDAX and TecDAX, and the relevant risk was therefore mid-cap semiconductor volatility rather than a small-cap liquidity problem. Order-book disappointments, guidance cuts and customer-capex pauses were still filtered through a German mid-cap technology register rather than the broader DAX 40, which helped explain why cyclical disappointments repeatedly produced outsized share-price reactions. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

Taken together, the six risk dimensions form an interlocking constraint on AIXTRON's forward earnings visibility: cyclicality determines revenue amplitude, China determines near-term volume, micro-LED determines the upside option, FX determines reported margin, competition determines long-term pricing power, and governance determines the rate at which the market discounts the residual uncertainty. None of these risks is novel to the business; what distinguishes the 2024–2026 period is their simultaneous activation across the same compressed window.

chapters.title: GaN power scaling, SiC ramp, photonics demand, 2026-2030 horizon
chapters.body:
## The G10 at Scale: GaN Power's Inflection Curve

By spring 2026, AIXTRON's G10-GaN platform had entered the installed-base accumulation phase of GaN power adoption. The transition was structural: GaN semiconductors were displacing silicon MOSFETs and IGBTs across EV onboard chargers, data-centre PSUs, and consumer fast-charging adapters.

Yet the adoption curve remained sensitive to end-market timing. European and North American automotive demand was consolidating into steady-state replenishment, while Chinese domestic GaN fabs added capacity at a pace informed as much by industrial policy as near-term device demand.

## SiC: The Second Front

By early 2026, SiC had become AIXTRON's most closely watched forward variable. The commercial case rested on process flexibility and customer-base overlap: device manufacturers running mixed GaN/SiC roadmaps could source epitaxy equipment from a single vendor.

Wolfspeed's capital-intensity challenges and broader SiC supply-chain recalibration created an ambiguous demand backdrop. Grawert framed the opportunity as a multi-year ramp — a disciplined positioning against a qualification cycle stretching twelve to eighteen months.

## Photonics: The Quiet Growth Vector

The photonics franchise attracted less investor attention than power electronics, but by 2026 it had emerged as a more consistent revenue contributor. The AI infrastructure build-out drove demand: 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers required high volumes of GaAs and InP laser diodes.

Automotive LiDAR provided diversification: the shift to solid-state architectures increased laser-diode content per vehicle.

| Segment | Substrate | Tool platform | Principal demand driver (2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GaN power electronics | GaN-on-Si, GaN-on-SiC | G10-GaN | EV onboard chargers, data-centre PSU |
| SiC power devices | 4H-SiC | G10-SiC | EV traction inverters, industrial drives |
| Datacom laser diodes | GaAs, InP | G5/G10 optoelectronics | AI cluster interconnect, 800G/1.6T |
| Automotive LiDAR | GaAs, InP | G5/G10 optoelectronics | ADAS Level 3+ solid-state sensors |
| VCSEL / 3D sensing | GaAs | G5 | Consumer depth sensing |
| Micro-LED display | InGaN / GaN-on-sapphire | Specialised platform | Speculative; programme delays |

## The Micro-LED Residual Option

Management positioned Micro LED as an option rather than a plan, avoiding the trap of embedding speculative display demand into guidance. The asymmetry remained real — a genuine production ramp would still matter — but AIXTRON's own 2024 report had already moved the commercial timetable out by two to three years, and the 2025 mix data showed that display was no longer carrying the base case. [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2025](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2025/en/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf)

## The 2026–2030 Horizon

Standing at the frozen snapshot date, AIXTRON's strategic posture was defined by three structural convictions and one open question. The convictions: that GaN power electronics would continue migrating from design-win phase into volume production, sustaining multi-year installed-base expansion for the G10-GaN platform; that SiC would graduate from qualification-phase revenue into a commercially material product line, with timing contingent on the customer qualification outcomes seeded in 2024 and 2025; and that photonics demand — anchored by the AI data-centre interconnect build — would provide a revenue floor through any near-term power-electronics inventory correction.

The open question remained Micro LED. The April 2026 guidance raise was driven by optoelectronics, not by display, and neither the guidance update nor the subsequent Q1 statement relied on any display-scale recovery. That conservatism was appropriate given AIXTRON's own warning that Micro LED launches had slipped, and it meant that any future display-scale procurement would still sit outside the base case. [AIXTRON guidance update](https://aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20SE%20increases%20FY%202026%20guidance%20and%20reports%20preliminary%20Q1/2026%20figures_n13936) [Q1/2026 Quarterly Statement](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2026/englisch/3-Months-Report-2026.pdf) [AIXTRON Annual Report 2024](https://www.aixtron.com/investoren/publikationen/2024/en/Annual%20Report%202024.pdf)

The capital cycle governing all of this was ultimately a function of device manufacturers' willingness to commit fab expansion capex — and AIXTRON, as a tool supplier rather than a chip producer, had no direct exposure to semiconductor end demand. That positioning was the source of both its leverage and its characteristic cyclicality. When GaN and SiC device fabs expanded capacity, AIXTRON's order intake moved first; when fabs paused to digest installed capacity, revenue compressed. The structural argument for the 2026–2030 period was that the demand base had become meaningfully more distributed than the LED MOCVD era had delivered: multiple end markets, multiple geographies, multiple substrate technologies operating on partially uncorrelated investment timelines. Whether that diversification would produce a smoother capital cycle or merely a more complex one remained, as of the snapshot, the central empirical question for the years ahead.
